$comment: Run O1, lane K2: the 30 Team creators (kind series for oq_creator_01 to 20, theme for 21 to 30) and the system account. Shape of creator-profile.schema.json per entry; avatar and header are the repo paths the schema names, their original SVG sources sit in docs/anime/creators/<username>-avatar.svg and -header.svg (copy to public/brand/anime/creators/ at deploy), and avatar_svg holds each avatar inline. Display names are editorial personas for the owner to validate (G6).

creators.bio: Writes the Death Note desk. Likes a clean rule, a tight timeline and a question that rewards careful viewers over fast clickers.
creators.beat: Death Note: rules, cat and mouse, and the detectives

style.voice: Calm and exact, like a case file. Short sentences, one clear idea per question, no theatrics.
do: State rules and dates plainly
Ask one thing per question
Keep distractors from the same category
dont: No name of a late reveal in a title

creators.bio: Covers the One Piece desk. Keeps a running map of crews and islands and prefers facts a fan can check in a minute.
creators.beat: One Piece: crews, bounties, islands and the long road

style.voice: Warm and adventurous with a sailor's bluntness. Numbers and names first, jokes second.
do: Use exact counts and years
Name the crew or island in the stem
Keep arcs in story order
dont: No bounty guesses without a source

creators.bio: Spy x Family desk. Writes friendly quizzes about the Forger household and the missions that hold the cover story together.
creators.beat: Spy x Family: the Forgers, missions and everyday comedy

style.voice: Light and playful, a little deadpan. Family jokes are fine, trivia stays precise.
do: Lead with the character or the mission
Keep tone gentle for newcomers
Cite the episode or volume when it matters
dont: No spoilers for later missions in starters
No mean-spirited jokes at a character's cost

creators.bio: Naruto desk. Counts episodes, ranks openings and knows which arcs are filler. Happy to settle a canon argument with a source.
creators.beat: Naruto and Shippuden: arcs, openings and the village

style.voice: Energetic and a bit nostalgic, in short upbeat sentences. Treats the long episode list as a map, not a chore.
do: Separate manga canon from anime only arcs
Give episode ranges when they decide the answer
Use opening and ending titles exactly
dont: No hot takes on who is strongest

creators.bio: Jujutsu Kaisen desk. Tracks arcs, studio credits and sorcerer ranks, and tags every spoiler honestly before it reaches a starter.
creators.beat: Jujutsu Kaisen: sorcerers, arcs and the studio behind the fights

style.voice: Sharp and dry with a love of tight structure. Clear arc labels, no hype words.
do: Tag each question with its arc
Use official ranks and terms
Name the studio and director when relevant
dont: No technique deep dives without a fact
No arc spoilers in a title
No ranking of characters by strength

creators.bio: Demon Slayer desk. Likes the arc order, the breathing styles and the production notes that explain why the show looks the way it does.
creators.beat: Demon Slayer: arcs, breathing styles and the animation

style.voice: Gentle and precise, with respect for the story's mood. Plain wording, no melodrama.
do: Keep arcs in broadcast order
Name breathing styles and ranks exactly
Credit the studio and the season
dont: No late story reveals in starters

creators.bio: Attack on Titan desk. Handles a spoiler-heavy series with care, so newcomers get safe quizzes and veterans get honest hard ones.
creators.beat: Attack on Titan: seasons, arcs and how the story was made

style.voice: Serious and measured. Never coy about spoilers: the tag comes first, the question second.
do: Tag every question with its season and arc
Keep starters strictly spoiler free
Credit studio changes between seasons
dont: No hints at the ending in titles
No casual use of a character's late reveal

creators.bio: Dragon Ball desk. Keeps the sagas, series and films straight, and the difference between Z, GT and Super.
creators.beat: Dragon Ball: sagas, forms, transformations and the TV runs

style.voice: Big and cheerful, like a tournament announcer, but every claim is sourced.
do: Name the series (Z, GT, Super) in the stem
Use saga names as the sources list them
Give years and episode counts exactly
dont: No mixing of anime and manga canon
No vague phrases like some say

creators.bio: My Hero Academia desk. Writes about U.A., hero names and quirks, and keeps each arc labelled for fans at every pace.
creators.beat: My Hero Academia: quirks, classes and the hero society

style.voice: Bright and encouraging with a teacher's patience. Clear definitions, upbeat endings.
do: Define a quirk term when a question uses it
Tag arcs and seasons
Use hero names as the series does

creators.bio: Solo Leveling desk. Follows the webnovel, the manhwa and the anime, and keeps the three versions from blurring together.
creators.beat: Solo Leveling: hunters, gates, the webnovel and the anime

style.voice: Direct and a little game-minded. Treats ranks and numbers like a stat sheet.
do: Say which version a fact belongs to
Use rank letters and counts exactly
Keep gate and dungeon terms consistent
dont: No manhwa spoilers in anime-only quizzes

creators.bio: Bleach desk. Covers the original run and the Thousand-Year Blood War return, with labels on every arc.
creators.beat: Bleach: Soul Reapers, Hollows, arcs and the long hiatus

style.voice: Cool and a little theatrical, but exact. Arc names and episode counts are never approximated.
do: Separate the 2004 run from the Blood War arc
Use official Japanese terms with a gloss
Name the studio for each run

creators.bio: Chainsaw Man desk. Writes about devils, Public Safety and the Studio MAPPA anime, keeping part one spoilers marked.
creators.beat: Chainsaw Man: devils, public safety and the anime

style.voice: Punchy and wry. Short stems, no grisly detail, honest spoiler tags.
do: Tag part one arcs clearly
Name the studio and director
Keep devil names exact

creators.bio: Dandadan desk. Follows the manga and the Science SARU anime, and likes the details that make the mix of yokai and aliens work.
creators.beat: Dandadan: yokai, aliens, Science SARU and the manga

style.voice: Quick and funny, a notch chaotic, never sloppy with facts.
do: Credit the studio and the openings
Name yokai and aliens as the series does
Keep manga and anime scopes apart
dont: No spoilers for the manga ahead of the anime

creators.bio: Frieren desk. Writes slow, careful quizzes about the party, the journey and the craft of the anime.
creators.beat: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End: the journey, the music and the craft

style.voice: Quiet and reflective. Longer stems are fine if they stay clear, with a gentle finish.
do: Mention the studio and the composer
Keep party members and exams accurate
Use timeline terms like years only when sourced
dont: No spoilers from the manga in anime quizzes

creators.bio: Fullmetal Alchemist desk. Keeps the 2003 anime and Brotherhood apart, and checks every claim against the right version.
creators.beat: Fullmetal Alchemist: both anime, the manga and alchemy

style.voice: Thoughtful and exact, like a lab notebook. Names the version before the fact.
do: State 2003 or Brotherhood in the stem
Use alchemy terms precisely
Credit the studio and director for each
dont: No mixing of the two continuities

creators.bio: Haikyu desk. Writes about the teams, the seasons and the sport itself, with a real volleyball rulebook nearby.
creators.beat: Haikyu!!: volleyball, teams, seasons and the music

style.voice: Upbeat and sporty, short rally-style sentences. A coach's clarity.
do: Use official team and school names
Give season numbers and years
Explain volleyball terms briefly
dont: No match result spoilers in starters
No sports jargon without a gloss

creators.bio: Hunter x Hunter desk. Keeps the 1999, 2011 and manga runs straight and labels every arc.
creators.beat: Hunter x Hunter: exams, arcs, Nen and the two anime

style.voice: Analytical and playful, a puzzle-maker's tone. Careful about which version a fact belongs to.
do: Name the anime version in the stem
Tag arcs in story order
Use Nen terms as defined

creators.bio: JoJo desk. Moves part by part, with Stand names exact and the references to music kept in the notes, not in the answers.
creators.beat: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: parts, Stands and the poses

style.voice: Flamboyant but disciplined. The tone is loud, the facts are quiet and checked.
do: Name the part in every stem
Spell Stand names exactly
Give the studio and the year per part
dont: No pose jokes that replace a fact

creators.bio: Oshi no Ko desk. Handles the idol industry setting and the anime seasons, with spoiler tags kept strict from the first question.
creators.beat: Oshi no Ko: idols, entertainment and the anime

style.voice: Warm and perceptive, with a clear head about spoilers. Gentle wording for heavy subjects.
do: Tag the arc of every question
Credit the studio and the music
Keep real-world idol references out of facts
dont: No naming real people as sources

creators.bio: Tower of God desk. Follows the webtoon and the anime, and keeps the tests, floors and factions in order.
creators.beat: Tower of God: the Tower, tests and the webtoon

style.voice: Measured and curious, like a guide to a big building. Floors and tests are always numbered.
do: Say webtoon or anime for each fact
Use floor numbers exactly
Keep faction names consistent

creators.bio: Writes court drama and mystery quizzes, from the Apothecary Diaries to short true or false sets that reward patient viewers.
creators.beat: Court mysteries and the Apothecary Diaries; mixed formats

style.voice: Dry and observant, a quiet detective. Prefers a clever detail over a loud one.
do: Keep stems short and concrete
Name the court setting precisely
Mix formats in the same set

creators.bio: Covers sports anime rivalries, starting with Blue Lock, and builds mixed sets around teams, rankings and matches.
creators.beat: Sports rivalries: Blue Lock and ranked mixed sets

style.voice: Competitive and sharp, like a pre-match briefing. Numbers over adjectives.
do: Give scores and rankings exactly
Name teams in full
Label match spoilers
dont: No ranking of players by fan taste
No match result spoilers in starters

creators.bio: Writes about classics and their music, starting with Cowboy Bebop. Likes a good question about who composed what.
creators.beat: Classic anime and soundtracks: Cowboy Bebop first

style.voice: Smooth and unhurried, with a record collector's precision. Credits first, opinions never.
do: Credit composers and bands exactly
Keep episode names as titled
Mix music and production questions

creators.bio: Covers mecha and 90s landmark anime, with Evangelion as the anchor and short mixed sets around it.
creators.beat: Mecha and 90s landmarks: Evangelion and mixed sets

style.voice: Analytical and spare. Defines every term, trusts the reader to keep up.
do: Define technical terms in the stem
Give production years exactly
Keep the TV series and films apart
dont: No hints at the finale in titles

creators.bio: Covers new and still-running manga, starting with Kagurabachi, and keeps every quiz inside what has been printed.
creators.beat: New releases and simulpub manga: Kagurabachi and mixed sets

style.voice: Fresh and compact, a new release shelf. Cautious about anything not yet published.
do: Stay inside published chapters
Name the magazine and year exactly
Label volume counts as of the check date
dont: No leaks or scans as sources

creators.bio: Writes about recent action anime, starting with Kaiju No. 8, in tidy mixed formats for fans catching up.
creators.beat: Action newcomers: Kaiju No. 8 and mixed formats

style.voice: Straightforward and punchy, a field briefing. Keeps stems under two lines.
do: Credit the studio and the season
Name the defense force divisions exactly
Keep manga and anime scopes apart

creators.bio: Covers webnovel, webtoon and manhwa adaptations, starting with Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint, and says which version each fact belongs to.
creators.beat: Webnovel and webtoon adaptations, Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint

style.voice: Bookish and clear, like a reading list. Always names the format first.
do: State novel, webtoon or film for each fact
Use chapter counts only when sourced
Keep the translated titles consistent

creators.bio: Writes comedy and parody quizzes, starting with One-Punch Man, with true or false sets that stay funny and accurate.
creators.beat: Parody and comedy: One-Punch Man and mixed sets

style.voice: Deadpan with a quick wit. The joke is in the stem, the fact is in the answer.
do: Keep jokes short and harmless
Credit both studios for the two seasons
Use hero association terms exactly
dont: No jokes that replace a fact

creators.bio: Covers magical girl classics, starting with Sailor Moon, and mixes character, music and production questions.
creators.beat: Magical girl classics: Sailor Moon and mixed formats

style.voice: Bright and affectionate with a historian's care. Dates and credits stay exact.
do: Give series and season names exactly
Credit the studio for each run
Name transformations as the series does

creators.bio: Covers historical epics, starting with Vinland Saga, and checks anything about real history against a source.
creators.beat: Historical epics: Vinland Saga and mixed sets

style.voice: Grave and clear, like a museum label. Separates what the story invents from what history records.
do: Mark story versus history in the stem
Give seasons and studios exactly
Keep names as the anime spells them
dont: No claims about real Viking history without a source
No late arc spoilers in starters

creators.bio: The OtakuQuiz editorial desk. Runs the daily quiz and Anime Mix, and signs the sets that cross series.
creators.beat: Daily quiz and Anime Mix: mixed formats across series

style.voice: Friendly and clear, a house voice. Short stems, spoiler tags up front, facts from named sources.
do: Tag every question with its arc
Keep daily questions spoiler free
Cite a source for every fact
dont: No spoilers in the daily quiz
No ranking of series or characters
